note: Starter notes are short summaries of points that come up again and again when players talk about these lines. They were compiled by AI from general knowledge and retailer descriptions, not copied from any post. Real quotes with links replace them as the aggregator collects posts (see data/community.json).

families.name: Tantrum
notes: Easton's widest slowpitch line, so it comes in one-piece, two-piece, balanced, loaded and senior versions.
Break-in reports vary: some say it is ready early, others say it took a few hundred swings.
The Gold version is alloy, which suits players who want durability and no break-in.

families.name: Alpha
notes: Built with Resmondo input. The one-piece is known as a stiff bat with a lot of feedback.
Usually priced a little under Easton's flagship models.

families.name: Hype Fire
notes: Uses the composite from Easton's Hype baseball bats.
Newer to slowpitch, so there is less long-term durability talk so far.

families.name: Marsh
notes: Loaded USSSA model in one-piece and two-piece versions.

families.name: Power Brigade
notes: Compact one-piece, loaded. Released fall 2026.

families.name: Thing
notes: Two-piece loaded USSSA bat. Often on sale well under list price.

families.name: Stealth
notes: Revived name on a 2027 one-piece end-loaded USSSA bat.

families.name: Ronin
notes: Alloy and dual-stamped, so it is legal in both USA and USSSA play.
Players often buy it as a backup, a cold-weather bat or a first bat because alloy needs no break-in.
Expect less pop than a broken-in composite.

families.name: Rival
notes: Entry-level alloy with a dual stamp. A rec-league bat.

families.name: Empire (Senior)
notes: Easton's SSUSA senior line, with Greg Connell and Dennis Rulli signature models.

families.name: Twisted Mistress
notes: DeMarini's best-known end-loaded USSSA power bat, sold in several versions.
The 2027 mid-load version suits hitters who find the full end-load too heavy.

families.name: Standard / Standard Issue
notes: Lower-priced DeMarini USSSA option.

families.name: The Culture
notes: USSSA two-piece in DeMarini's 2026 and 2027 lineups.

families.name: Vanilla Gorilla
notes: Jason Magnum signature USSSA model.

families.name: Mercy / Merciless
notes: The Mercy is DeMarini's balanced USA model and is often suggested for rec and church leagues.
The Merciless is the end-loaded version.

families.name: Juggy
notes: Long-running DeMarini USA line. Extended means a longer barrel.

families.name: Flipper
notes: USA-stamped DeMarini power model.

families.name: CornDog (wood composite)
notes: Maple wood composite with a dual stamp. It is about as durable as slowpitch bats get.
Popular for batting practice, cold-weather games and wood-bat tournaments.
Much less pop than a hot composite.

families.name: Uprising
notes: Dual-stamp DeMarini value bat.

families.name: Freak
notes: One of the most talked-about USSSA lines. The Maxload (about 0.5 oz end-load) versions are aimed at power hitters.
Miken releases many paint schemes each year. Players often point out that several share the same platform underneath.
Comes in 12" to 14" barrels, in one-piece and two-piece.

families.name: KP23
notes: Kyle Pearson signature line, sold in 12.5" two-piece and 14" one-piece versions.

families.name: MV1
notes: 13" Maxload USSSA bat, new in fall 2026.

families.name: HB12
notes: 12.5" end-loaded USSSA model with a retro paint job.

families.name: Vicious (alloy)
notes: Dual-stamp alloy that budget guides often pick first.
It should not crack the way composite does, but it has less pop than Miken's composites.

families.name: Ultra Gamer (Senior)
notes: SSUSA senior bat in Maxload and Supermax versions. Often discounted.

families.name: Bedlam
notes: Worth's core two-piece line. XL means about a 0.5 oz end-load and XXL means heavier.
The Bedlam XL USA is the only USA-stamped bat in Worth's 2026 core lineup.

families.name: Krecher / Silverback
notes: One-piece Worth USSSA bats, so they feel stiffer than two-pieces.

families.name: Legit
notes: Comes in USSSA and USA versions, one-piece and two-piece.

families.name: Thumper
notes: 13.5" two-piece end-loaded USSSA bat with a wood-look finish.

families.name: AMP (alloy)
notes: Cheapest dual-stamp option here. Fine for casual rec play.

families.name: Genesis
notes: Louisville Slugger's main USSSA line, with many signature and paint versions.
Sits at the premium end of USSSA prices.
2026 versions use a double-wall barrel and the QWK 2.0 two-piece connection.

families.name: Trippin'
notes: Monsta's 2026 USSSA two-piece, priced well under most big-brand USSSA bats. It often sells out.

families.name: Torch
notes: Monsta's best-known USA bat. Its MX composite is often called a premium choice for USA play.
Monsta is a smaller brand, so expect pre-orders and stock gaps.

families.name: DNA / King of Diamonds
notes: Other Monsta USA composites in the same family as the Torch.

families.name: Melee (Senior)
notes: Comes up constantly in senior softball talk.
Stamped SSUSA and ISA only, so it is not legal in USA or USSSA adult leagues.

families.name: Vibe / Nox
notes: Victus is a baseball wood brand that recently moved into slowpitch.
Ya-Ya Load is their name for an end-load.

families.name: Fury Bravo
notes: Sold with either the oval Axe handle or a conventional flared handle. Players tend to love or hate the Axe handle, so try one first if you can.
Stamped USSSA, NSA and ISA.

families.name: Dabacle
notes: Dual-stamp balanced Axe model.

families.name: Rckless Resmondo
notes: Marucci's slowpitch line, built with Resmondo. Launched September 2026.
Stamped USSSA, NSA and ISA. Available in one-piece and two-piece.

families.name: Gridlock
notes: Marucci's loaded USA model.

families.name: Groovy
notes: Balanced two-piece in USSSA and senior versions.

families.name: Omen / PTSD Awareness (Senior)
notes: End-loaded senior model.

families.name: Rocketech
notes: Long-running Anderson alloy with a dual stamp. A durable, no-break-in bat.

families.name: Stadium
notes: 13" end-loaded USSSA two-piece, sold in 2026 and 2027 versions.

families.name: Kingpin (Senior)
notes: DeMarini's one-piece SSUSA senior bat.

families.name: CAT 1776
notes: Loaded USA model released for the country's 250th anniversary.

families.name: Beacon
notes: Victus's first slowpitch line. Mostly one-piece with a Ya-Ya end-load, plus a heavier Big Boy Load version.

families.name: CR-1 Bradley Jones
notes: Combat is back in slowpitch with three CR-1 versions, all with a 0.5 oz end-load. The two-piece is said to sting less.
